text: Have you ever been to Peru?
Where have you been this year?
I have been there twice.
How long have you been here?

I have been to forty-seven countries. People ask me how that is possible. It is simple. I never stay long. Last year I visited six countries in one month. I went to Peru, Chile and Argentina by bus. I have slept in airports. I have missed trains. I have eaten things I could not name. And every place gave me a story. When I meet somebody in a bar, I always ask the same question: where have you been? Because the answer tells me who you are. So my advice is this. Go now, go fast, and see as much as you can. You can rest when you get home.

I have only been to nine countries, and I am happy with that. Two years ago I spent three months in a small town in Italy. I did not visit anything famous. I bought bread from the same man every morning. By the end, he knew my name, and I knew the names of his kids. That trip changed me more than ten fast trips. So when people ask me where I have been, I prefer a different question: where have you stayed? Fast travel gives you photos. Slow travel gives you friends. And honestly, is that not the reason we travel?
